Q: select count from a select? A:

You get the number of different lenses used per camera model with

select model, count(distinct lens) as number_of_different_lenses
from tb_exifinfo
group by model;

In the request comments you say you solved your problem with the following query, though:

with
  a as 
  (
    select model, count(distinct lens) N 
    from tb_exifinfo
    group by model
    order by model
  ),
  b as 
  (
    select model, max(N) as maxN
    from a
    group by model
  )
select a.model, a.N 
from a 
join b on a.model=b.model and a.N=b.maxN;

This query is overly complicated.

  1. In a you get the number of lenses per model, i.e. one row per model. The ORDER BY clause is superfluous here.
  2. Then, in b, you say "from those rows (one per model) give me one row per model". This makes no sense. You get the same rows, only that what you called N before, you call maxN now. Same rows, same data, only another column name, because the maximum of a set of one value is the value itself of course.
  3. Now you join a and b, which of course gives you the same data again, only with duplicated columns.

So, replace your query with the simple one I have mentioned above. Add an ORDER BY clause at its end to get the rows in the order you desire.
